title: HPTLC approach for determining withaferin A in polyherbal formulations and extracts from  Withania somnifera  characterized by greenness, blueness, and whiteness profiles
content: Commercially available polyherbal formulations (PHFs) of Withania somnifera extract are used for the treatment of various diseases such as cardiovascular and neurological disorders. There are no documented greener normal-phase high-performance thin-layer chromatographic (NP-HPTLC) methods in the literature for detecting withaferin A in PHFs. Thus, the purpose of the present investigation was to establish and validate a green NP-HPTLC method for determining withaferin A in methanol extracts of the roots, stems, and leaves of W. somnifera grown in Saudi Arabia as well as commercially available PHFs. The wavelength at which withaferin A was identified was 223 nm. The binary mixture of ethanol and cyclohexane (60 : 40 v/v) was used as the development system. The greenness, blueness, and whiteness profiles of the suggested withaferin A analytical approach were evaluated using eight different tools, including “the analytical eco-scale (AES), chloroform toxicity (ChlorTox), analytical GREEnness (AGREE), the modified green analytical procedure index (MoGAPI), the complex MoGAPI, the blue applicability grade index (BAGI), the carbon footprint reduction index (CaFRI), and the click analytical chemistry index (CACI)”. In the 25–1000 ng per band range, the current withaferin A analytical method demonstrated linearity (R2 = 0.9968, n = 6). Additionally, the withaferin A analytical method was sensitive (LOD = 8.42 ng per band and LOQ = 25.28 ng per band), robust, accurate (% recoveries = 98.58–100.85), precise (% CV = 0.77–0.99), and sustainable in standard solutions. Using the proposed withaferin A analytical method, the findings of AES (85), ChlorTox (2.00 g), AGREE (0.73), MoGAPI (82), complex MoGAPI (88), BAGI (85), CaFRI (88), and CACI (90) indicated the outstanding greenness, blueness, and whiteness profiles. It was observed that marketed PHFs P1, P2, P3, and P4 contained, respectively, 0.70, 0.03, 0.62, and 0.06% w/w of withaferin A in the dried extract. The amount of withaferin A in extracts of roots, stems, and leaves of W. somnifera was determined to be 0.16, 0.32, and 0.36% w/w of the dried extract, respectively. According to the study's findings, the current green NP-HPTLC technology can be used to regularly monitor withaferin A in commercialized PHFs and other extracts of W. somnifera.
